# 油價回落帶動美債反彈，財政部融資需求卻上升

## 美伊外交進展帶回債市買盤

美伊外交出現新進展，油價大跌，帶動美債收復週五大部分失地，股市也同步上漲。美國總統川普取消原定攻擊，伊朗則表示恢復荷莫茲海峽航運已有進展。布蘭特原油下跌6.95%至$83.86，WTI下跌5.14%至$80.32。

10年期美債殖利率下降5個基點至4.70%，其中4個基點來自實質殖利率，後者收在2.43%。2年期下降3個基點至4.25%，30年期下降4個基點至5.23%。S&P 500上漲1.48%。股債齊揚，反映能源與地緣政治風險減輕，而不是投資人因擔心成長惡化而尋求避險。

美國國內的政策與融資消息卻沒有同樣輕鬆。紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams預期下半年通膨放緩，但若未朝2%目標前進，仍不排除進一步行動。市場給予9月升息約70%的機率。財政部則在不提高現金餘額目標的情況下，將本季借款預估增加$680億至$7,390億。

公債殖利率下降，也未帶動美國企業債基金上漲。信用較弱的借款人面對截然不同的結果：寮國EDL-Generation以11.125%票息完成罕見的CCC級美元債發行，中國一家城投公司因定價問題延後再融資，Hughes Satellite則在8月債務到期前聲請破產。週一基準利率的下降減輕了融資負擔，但各發行人能取得資金的條件仍相差甚遠。

## Williams主張觀望，財政部需要更多資金

5年期與10年期美債領漲，殖利率各降5個基點至4.40%、4.70%。兩端降幅較小，2s10s因此收窄2個基點至45，2s30s收窄1個基點至98。不過，10年期殖利率仍比一週前高5個基點、比一個月前高21個基點；30年期則分別高11及25個基點。

抗通膨債也只收復部分失地。10年期實質殖利率下降4個基點至2.43%，損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點至2.27%，實質殖利率仍比一個月前高17個基點。油價下跌減輕眼前的通膨風險，但當日名目殖利率降幅主要來自實質折現率下降，而不是中長期通膨補償同步大幅回落。

Williams的發言，與週五三名聯準會異議官員的升息理由形成對照。他認為目前利率位置適當，預期下半年通膨下降，並在2028年持續回到2%。但他也表示，若經濟未朝此目標前進，聯準會就應採取行動。在週五公布的季度就業成本增幅達0.9%、高於預期之後，這項保留仍有分量：市場給予9月升息近70%的機率，至10月則幾乎完全計入25個基點的升幅。

爭論不只在下一次行動的時間。主席Kevin Warsh認為，市場殖利率提高已在緊縮金融情勢。Citadel Securities指出其中可能形成循環：聯準會選擇等待，使長期借款成本上升；長期成本上升，又成為聯準會繼續等待的理由。如果殖利率上升反映的是投資人對通膨及政策架構的不安，依賴這種市場緊縮，反而可能強化最初的疑慮。

週一股債齊漲，比會後的市場反應友善，但財政部的新借款預估帶來另一項壓力。本季預估由$6,710億提高至$7,390億，主要因預期淨現金流減少。9月底現金餘額目標仍為$9,500億，代表調整來自融資需求提高，而非希望保留更大的現金緩衝。

交易商多半預期，週三季度再融資公告會維持未來至少幾季不增加中長期付息券標售規模的指引。更難回答的是，這項安排能維持多久。若付息券規模直到2027財政年度都不變，國庫券占未償債務比率可能升至25%，是危機期間以外少見的水準。約$8.3兆貨幣市場基金提供龐大的潛在需求，但更依賴短債，也使政府融資成本更容易受到未來升息影響。

摩根大通先前估計，若標售規模不變，2027至2030財政年度累計融資缺口達$3.7兆，因為每次發行愈來愈多資金須用於償還到期債務。部分交易商預期首次增加付息券規模落在2027年5月，另有機構認為指引可能保留2月就調整的空間。考量10年、20年及30年期殖利率已高，未來增發可能偏向短中天期。即使近期規模不變能暫時安撫市場，後續供給仍可能落在週一領漲的年期。

## 有人高價完成再融資，有人走向重整

美國企業債基金落後於公債和股市：LQD下跌0.13%，HYG下跌0.21%，JNK下跌0.24%。LQD近一個月仍跌2.33%，高收益基金則約跌0.5%。存續期間仍是整體報酬的重要負擔，但個別融資案更清楚呈現了信用條件及市場准入的差異。

寮國國營發電商EDL-Generation發行$3億5年期美元債，3年後可提前贖回，票息11.125%。資金將用於償還9月2日到期債券及其他債務，公司到2027年共有$3.78億到期。排除困境債務交換，2000年以來很少亞洲發行人能以低於B級的評等發行美元債。這筆CCC級交易完成之際，亞洲企業高收益債今年發行已逾$110億，比2025年同期高約50%，有望創2021年以來最旺的一年。需求確實存在，但這家公司仍須支付雙位數成本，且用途是再融資，而非擴張。

Luoyang Shangdu City Investment則無法與買方談攏價格。這家河南城投公司延後364天期境外人民幣債發行，並表示現有現金足以償還8月11日到期的兩筆債券，合計CNY10.8億、票息分別為6.9%及7.9%。這是對流動性的保證，尚不是已完成的替代融資。

公司公布收入CNY2.5億、獲利CNY1,600萬，資產負債率67.33%；另曾列入法院被執行人名單，4月底逾期款項為CNY1,000萬。中國支持措施已使2027年6月前到期城投債的融資成本降至紀錄低點，但全產業CNY16兆未償債券中，仍有CNY5兆在2027年底前到期。政策支持沒有消除買方對較弱發行人的價格要求，尤其當政策也不鼓勵高成本境外融資時。

Hughes Satellite則已越過再融資談判階段。這家EchoStar子公司警告現金不足以履約後，於週日依美國破產法第11章聲請重整。申報資產及負債各介於$10億至$100億，8月到期債務達$15億。母公司先前表示可能不再提供新資金，迫近的到期壓力因此轉由重整程序處理。

紐約住宅市場也出現債權處置進展。JPMCC 2021-NYAH債券持有人加強推動抵押權實行；這筆$5.06億CMBS以53棟租金穩定管制住宅為擔保，逾期利息超過$550萬。KBRA Credit Profile估計物業價值約$4.6億，低於發行時的$7.17億，債券持有人可能損失逾$8,000萬。10月凍漲租金又限制了收入成長，而費用仍持續增加。

問題早在凍租之前就已累積。原本只付息的浮動利率房貸設有利率上限，使實際成本維持在約3.66%，大致為後來失去避險保護時的一半。到2024年貸款到期時，營運費用比預期高13%，每$1本息支出僅有$0.58現金流可支應。借款人停止部分付款後，服務機構已墊付約$2,900萬。面額$3,100萬的次順位券價格約為面額49%，其上方$4,700萬券別約為64%。穆迪估計，若長期凍租，紐約市CMBS多戶住宅貸款約6%可能面臨違約；其他組合中的市價租金收入則可限制損失。壓力最集中的仍是浮動債務、高槓桿與管制收入同時存在的物業。

AI融資帶來的是另一種挑戰：投資組合須為較強信用及具增信安排的債務騰出空間。全球市場已吸收約$5,700億AI相關債務，Citadel Securities另估計，至2028年用於晶片融資的新增公私募借款可能超過$5,000億，其中2028年單是晶片商就可能超過$2,500億。為配合設備壽命，許多債務可能採3至5年期，壓力因此不只在長天期供給，也在較短年期投資組合的承接能力。

既有交易顯示，這些債務如何進入投資級買方的範圍。美國市場自去年以來吸收約$600億短天期大型雲端業者債務。Anthropic取得約$350億融資購買Google客製化晶片，由Broadcom為優先順位部分提供付款支持。這可改善特定券別的評等，但投資人仍須評估保證人、設備價值及技術淘汰風險。若供給達到預測規模，可能迫使投資組合減持其他科技、媒體及電信債券。

韓國借款人則已轉向短期資金。金融及非金融企業上半年商業本票發行達KRW282.8兆，年增19%；短期債券發行年增90.4%至KRW990.1兆。股市熱絡時證券商需要資本，長端殖利率提高也促使企業縮短借款年期。但Kospi在7月下跌22%之後，更大的短期再融資需求，正面對較弱的擔保品價值及交易環境。

保險業也把更多風險轉入債市。今年含野火曝險的巨災債發行超過$50億，同時野火保險損失約以每年12%的速度增加。整體巨災債發行在2025年成長45%，未償規模升至紀錄$610億。新增資金提高保險公司的損失承擔能力，也讓債券投資人直接面對災害事件及氣候損失模型的不確定性。

## 日本的美元需求，把匯率防衛連到美債供給

日本干預日圓，直接連結了匯率政策與美債供給。估計日本當局週五投入JPY5.33兆、約$340億，前一天操作規模更大。日本持有逾$1.1兆美債，若透過賣券取得美元，可能對美國殖利率增添壓力。

聯準會FIMA附買回機制提供另一條路：外國官方機構可用美債作擔保借入美元。每個交易對手每日上限$600億，只比上週其中一次干預的估計規模略高。美國財長Scott Bessent鼓勵聯準會提高上限，相關決定屬於FOMC外匯小組委員會的權責。

此前實際使用量很小。截至7月29日一週，平均餘額約$600萬，上一次較大規模使用是2月的$30億。融資利率為3.75%，7天期則按1週OIS加25個基點計價，高於民間附買回市場。這套機制可避免失序賣債，但若反覆干預，就須不斷展延成本較高的短期借款，無法取代匯率誘因的長期調整。日本銀行利率僅1%，仍遠低於美國；交換市場給予9月日本升息近50%的機率。

歐洲的討論則著重不確定性如何壓抑需求。研究發現，伊朗戰爭後歐元區家庭減少支出，主因是不確定性，而非立即對通膨作出反應。英國央行總裁Andrew Bailey認為，金融情勢收緊與向上傾斜的殖利率曲線能抑制初現的通膨壓力；ECB總裁Christine Lagarde也強調市場波動及風險趨避會削弱需求。油價回落減輕通膨威脅，但若信心跟著恢復，先前對支出的抑制也可能部分消退。

印度曲線轉陡的原因更具體：短端流動性充裕。6月推出的措施已吸引逾$400億，核心盧比流動性可能從6月底INR5兆增至12月INR10兆。5年期公債殖利率下降35個基點至6.45%，30年期僅降17個基點至7.47%，兩者利差擴大至100個基點以上。銀行把資金投入較短資產，全球通膨及供給疑慮卻限制長債漲幅。

印度央行預期維持利率，總裁Sanjay Malhotra認為通膨沒有全面加速。不過，優惠存款換匯窗口將在本季結束，這項流動性支持有明確期限。曲線轉陡反映的是短債獲得資金支撐，不必然代表央行將更鷹派。

香港境外避險產品則由計畫進入實際交易。現金結算的5年期中國公債期貨開始交易，合約面額CNY50萬，開盤價格與境內同類產品僅有小幅差異。中國5年期公債殖利率週五收在1.41%，為2025年2月以來最低。歷經2017年及2024年未能成功建立市場的嘗試後，接下來要看交易能否持續，使境外投資人不必調整現券部位就能可靠地避險。

## 非洲發行增加，阿根廷選擇等待

美元走強之際，新興市場美元債仍受惠於美債殖利率及油價下降。EMB上漲0.10%，15年期以上美元主權債指數上漲0.49%。但後者一週仍跌0.88%、一個月跌3.54%，當日反彈尚未彌補長存續期間部位的損失。

非洲政府持續取得融資。花旗2026年安排的主權交易達$62億，比去年同期增加約70%，已接近2025全年$73億。肯亞、安哥拉及象牙海岸都透過公募或私募取得資金，加彭最新交易籌得$9.2億。較早的美元弱勢及風險偏好有利再融資，但衝突若再升級，仍可能拖慢下半年發行。

官方支持也開拓其他管道。英國出口融資署保證支持奈及利亞Lagos及TinCan Island港口GBP7.46億重建計畫；連接坎帕拉與肯亞邊境的EUR27億鐵路也在推進，世界銀行可能參與。保證及多邊資金可讓長期建設在美債殖利率偏高時仍取得融資，但執行、匯率及完工風險仍須處理。

阿根廷則主動不接受外部市場的價格。估計投資人願提供至少$50億，但經濟部長Luis Caputo認為，約9%的要求殖利率不符合政府財政及通膨改革的成果。阿根廷改在國內發行美元計價債券，並取得由世界銀行及美洲開發銀行保證的$32億銀行貸款。

這些選項成本較低，等待的時間風險卻不小。淨外匯準備估計約$100億，$200億IMF計畫要求重建緩衝，2027年外幣付款又超過$250億。財政整頓、農業出口及Vaca Muerta收入都有幫助，但繼續等待，也使融資更依賴國內美元、多邊機構，以及可能因選舉而轉差的未來市場窗口。

智利最重要的外部變數仍是油價。6月通膨加速至4.3%，高於3%目標。巴克萊估計，油價上漲10%，約推升3年期披索主權債殖利率5個基點。市場隱含一年後政策利率為4.73%，相對現有4.5%約等於升息25個基點，一個月前卻還預期降息。

週一油價回落若能持續，將減輕這項壓力。智利燃料穩定機制吸收部分國內外價差，財長已警告長期補貼無法持續。投資人轉向短期UF抗通膨債，調查中53%受訪者預期相關殖利率一個月內下降1至10個基點。持續的低油價，既有利通膨，也能降低政府保護消費者的財政成本。

巴西寬鬆預期則稍微延伸。央行每週調查把2026年底Selic利率預估由14%降至13.75%，通膨預估連續第5週下降至5.03%。市場仍預期決策者連續第4次降息25個基點至14%。通膨仍明顯高於3%目標，因此較像漸進降息，而非迅速脫離限制性利率。

## 股票參與反彈，企業債基金仍落後

S&P 500上漲1.48%，Nasdaq 100上漲1.78%，半導體指數上漲1.05%，VIX下降0.81%至15.86。連同美債反彈，這些變化顯示投資人歡迎地緣政治與能源風險減輕，而非為需求崩落作準備。

WTI收$80.32、布蘭特收$83.86，即使當日大跌，仍各比一個月前高約17%。10年期損益兩平通膨率只下降1個基點，調整遠小於油價。一次外交改善，尚未消除先前能源上漲留下的通膨影響。

黃金在股市上漲時仍升1.45%至$4,107.80，美元指數則在前一週下跌後回升0.22%至100.017。整體市場反彈，沒有使黃金需求消失。美國企業債基金小跌，與公債及新興市場美元債上漲形成對照，也最清楚顯示此次復甦並不全面：基準利率下降，尚未帶來一致的債市買盤。

## 先看季度再融資，再迎就業數據

財政部借款預估提高至$7,390億後，週三季度再融資公告將先登場。付息券規模不變，可延後眼前的供給增加；若措辭保留2027年2月、而非5月就調整的空間，下一次增發仍會更接近。這項指引與之後標售實際展現的需求，需要分開判讀。

8月7日就業報告，接著檢驗Williams主張的觀望空間，以及異議官員偏好的提早緊縮。市場預估新增非農就業85,000人，6月為57,000人，失業率維持4.2%。招聘更強，將支持目前約70%機率的9月升息預期；勞動需求轉弱，則給聯準會更多等待餘地。若實質殖利率也延續下降，而不只是能源價格帶來短暫紓解，債市反彈的基礎會更廣。

日本干預方式則是另一項美債風險。使用FIMA借款可限制直接賣債，但反覆使用這項設有上限的短期機制，也會顯示維持此策略的成本。除了日圓本身，下一次日本銀行會議及FIMA條件是否調整同樣重要。週一外交進展減輕了眼前油價衝擊，尚未解決日本如何籌措匯率防衛資金，以及本國利率會多快向海外靠攏。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Oil relief lifts Treasuries as borrowing needs climb

## Diplomacy brings buyers back to bonds

Treasuries recovered much of Friday's selloff as renewed US-Iran diplomacy sent oil sharply lower and gave investors room to buy bonds alongside equities. President Donald Trump called off a planned attack, while Iran indicated progress toward restoring shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent fell 6.95% to $83.86 and WTI dropped 5.14% to $80.32.

The ten-year Treasury yield declined 5 basis points to 4.70%, with 4 basis points of the move coming through the real yield, which closed at 2.43%. Two-year yields fell 3 basis points to 4.25% and the 30-year fell 4 to 5.23%. The S&P 500 gained 1.48%. The joint rally reflected relief from energy and geopolitical risk, rather than investors seeking safety from weaker growth.

Domestic policy and financing news offered less relief. New York Fed President John Williams expected inflation to ease in the second half but left open further action if it failed to move toward 2%. Markets still assigned roughly a 70% probability to a September hike. Treasury, meanwhile, raised its current-quarter borrowing estimate by $68 billion to $739 billion without increasing its cash target.

Lower government yields also failed to lift US corporate bond funds. At the weaker end of credit, Laos's EDL-Generation completed a rare triple-C dollar issue at 11.125%, a Chinese municipal borrower postponed refinancing over price, and Hughes Satellite entered bankruptcy with an August maturity approaching. Monday made benchmark borrowing costs less onerous; the terms on which individual borrowers could obtain financing remained much more varied.

## Williams offers patience; Treasury needs more cash

The five- and ten-year sectors led the rally, each falling 5 basis points to 4.40% and 4.70%. With smaller moves at either end, 2s10s flattened 2 basis points to 45 and 2s30s narrowed 1 to 98. Long yields nevertheless remained above recent levels: the ten-year was up 5 basis points over a week and 21 over a month, while the 30-year was up 11 and 25.

Inflation-linked bonds showed the same partial recovery. The ten-year real yield fell 4 basis points to 2.43%, against a 1-basis-point decline in the breakeven to 2.27%. Real yields were still 17 basis points higher over a month. Oil's decline reduced an immediate inflation risk, but most of Monday's nominal rally came from a lower real discount rate, not a comparable change in longer-run inflation compensation.

Williams supplied a patient counterweight to Friday's explanations from the three Fed dissenters. He described rates as well positioned, expected inflation to decline in the second half and projected a sustainable return to 2% in 2028. Yet he also said the Fed should act if the economy was not moving toward that goal. After Friday's stronger-than-expected 0.9% quarterly increase in employment costs, that qualification mattered: September hike odds remained near 70%, with a quarter-point increase almost fully priced by October.

The debate extends beyond the date of the next move. Chairman Kevin Warsh has argued that higher market yields are already tightening financial conditions. Citadel Securities identified a possible feedback loop: long borrowing costs rise because the Fed waits, and the Fed then waits because long borrowing costs have risen. If investors are demanding compensation for inflation or uncertainty about the policy framework, relying on that increase in yields can reinforce the concern that produced it.

Monday's stock-and-bond rally was less hostile to the Fed than the post-meeting reaction, but the financing outlook brought a separate reason for caution. Treasury lifted its current-quarter borrowing estimate from $671 billion to $739 billion, mainly because of lower expected net cash flows. The end-September cash target stayed at $950 billion, so the revision reflected a greater financing need rather than a larger desired buffer.

Dealers largely expected Wednesday's refunding announcement to retain guidance that note and bond auction sizes would stay unchanged for at least several quarters. The harder question was how long that could last. Keeping coupon sizes stable through fiscal 2027 could push bills toward 25% of outstanding debt, an unusually high share outside crises. Roughly $8.3 trillion in money-market funds offers a substantial buyer base, but greater reliance on short debt would also leave financing costs more sensitive to future policy-rate increases.

JPMorgan's previously outlined $3.7 trillion cumulative funding gap for fiscal 2027–2030 remains the scale of the problem at current auction sizes, as maturities absorb more of each sale. Some dealers now expected the first coupon increase around May 2027; others saw room for language allowing February. Eventual increases could favor short and intermediate maturities because ten-, 20- and 30-year yields were already elevated. That would place more supply in the sectors that led Monday's recovery, even if unchanged near-term guidance initially reassured investors.

## Refinancing succeeds at a price—or gives way to restructuring

US corporate funds lagged the Treasury and equity rally: LQD fell 0.13%, HYG 0.21% and JNK 0.24%. LQD remained down 2.33% over a month, compared with losses near 0.5% in the high-yield funds. Duration still accounted for an important part of the aggregate burden, while individual financings exposed sharper differences in creditworthiness and access.

EDL-Generation sold $300 million of five-year dollar notes, callable after three years, at an 11.125% coupon. The Laos state-owned power producer will use proceeds to repay a September 2 maturity and refinance other debt, with $378 million coming due through 2027. Excluding distressed exchanges, few Asian borrowers rated below single B have issued dollar bonds since 2000. Its completed triple-C deal came as Asian corporate high-yield issuance exceeded $11 billion, about 50% above the comparable 2025 period and on course for the busiest year since 2021. Buyers were available, but at a double-digit cost for refinancing rather than expansion.

Luoyang Shangdu City Investment could not agree a price. The Henan local-government financing vehicle postponed a 364-day offshore yuan issue, saying existing cash would cover CNY1.08 billion of two notes due August 11, carrying coupons of 6.9% and 7.9%. That was a liquidity assurance, not a completed replacement financing.

The issuer reported CNY16 million of profit on CNY250 million of revenue and liabilities equal to 67.33% of assets. It had appeared on a court enforcement list and had CNY10 million of overdue payments at end-April. China's support program has driven borrowing costs to record lows for LGFV debt maturing by June 2027, but CNY5 trillion of the sector's CNY16 trillion outstanding matures by end-2027. Support for the sector has not eliminated price resistance for its weaker borrowers, particularly as policy discourages expensive offshore debt.

Hughes Satellite had already moved beyond refinancing negotiations. The EchoStar unit filed for Chapter 11 on Sunday after warning that it lacked cash to meet obligations. It listed assets and liabilities each between $1 billion and $10 billion and had $1.5 billion of debt due in August. Its parent had indicated it might not provide new funds, leaving the impending maturity to be addressed through restructuring.

In New York housing, bondholders escalated foreclosure efforts on JPMCC 2021-NYAH, a $506 million CMBS backed by 53 rent-stabilized buildings. Past-due interest exceeded $5.5 million. KBRA Credit Profile valued the properties at about $460 million, down from $717 million at issuance, and estimated more than $80 million of bondholder losses. An October rent freeze now threatens recoveries by limiting revenue while expenses rise.

The deterioration began well before that freeze. The floating-rate, interest-only mortgage originally had a cap that kept its effective cost near 3.66%, roughly half the later unhedged rate. By its 2024 maturity, operating expenses were 13% above expectations and cash flow covered only $0.58 of each dollar of debt service. The servicer has advanced about $29 million since some borrower payments stopped. A $31 million junior tranche traded around 49 cents on the dollar and the next $47 million slice around 64 cents. Moody's estimated that a prolonged freeze could put 6% of New York City CMBS multifamily loans at risk of default, although exposure to market-rate rents limits losses elsewhere. The greatest pressure lies where floating debt, high leverage and regulated income coincide.

Prospective AI borrowing presents a different challenge: making room for supply from stronger credits and supported structures. Against roughly $570 billion of AI-related debt already absorbed globally, Citadel Securities estimated more than $500 billion of additional public and private borrowing by 2028 to finance chips. More than $250 billion could come from chipmakers in 2028 alone. Much may mature in three to five years to match equipment lives, bringing demand for portfolio capacity into shorter maturities rather than simply adding long-duration issuance.

Existing structures show how that debt can reach investment-grade buyers. US markets have absorbed about $60 billion of short-dated hyperscaler debt since last year. Anthropic secured roughly $35 billion for Google's custom chips, with Broadcom backstopping payments on senior portions. Such support can improve selected tranches' ratings, but leaves investors assessing guarantors, equipment values and technological obsolescence. The projected scale could require portfolios to reduce other technology, media and telecommunications holdings.

South Korean borrowers have already shifted toward short funding. Financial and nonfinancial commercial-paper issuance reached KRW282.8 trillion in the first half, up 19% from a year earlier; short-term bond issuance rose 90.4% to KRW990.1 trillion. Brokerages needed capital during the equity boom and higher long yields encouraged shorter borrowing. July's 22% Kospi decline leaves that larger refinancing requirement facing less supportive collateral values and trading conditions.

Insurers are also turning more risk into tradable debt. Wildfire-exposed catastrophe-bond issuance exceeded $5 billion during the year as insured wildfire losses grew about 12% annually. Total cat-bond issuance rose 45% in 2025, lifting the outstanding market to a record $61 billion. The additional capital gives insurers capacity to absorb losses while exposing bond investors directly to event risk and the uncertainty of climate-loss models.

## Japan's dollar needs connect currency defense to Treasuries

Japan's yen intervention creates a direct link between currency policy and Treasury supply. Authorities were estimated to have spent JPY5.33 trillion, or $34 billion, on Friday after an even larger operation the day before. With more than $1.1 trillion in Treasury holdings, Japan could raise dollars by selling securities, potentially adding pressure to US yields.

The Fed's FIMA repo facility offers an alternative: foreign authorities can obtain dollars against Treasury collateral. Its $60 billion daily counterparty limit is only modestly above the estimated size of one of last week's interventions. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent encouraged the Fed to raise that cap, a decision within the FOMC's foreign-currency subcommittee.

Usage had been small. Balances averaged about $6 million in the week through July 29, and the last material use was $3 billion in February. Funding costs 3.75%; seven-day access is priced at one-week OIS plus 25 basis points, above private repo. The facility could avert disorderly sales, but repeated intervention would require rolling relatively expensive short-term funding. It does not replace a lasting adjustment in currency incentives: the BOJ's 1% rate remains far below the US range, while swaps assigned nearly a 50% probability to a September Japanese increase.

Europe's policy discussion meanwhile turned on how uncertainty affects demand. Research found that euro-area households cut spending after the Iran war mainly because of uncertainty, rather than an immediate response to inflation. BOE Governor Andrew Bailey has argued that tighter financial conditions and an upward-sloping curve restrain emerging inflation; ECB President Christine Lagarde has similarly emphasized weaker demand in volatile, risk-averse markets. Oil relief can ease the inflation threat, but a recovery in confidence could also reverse some of that restraint on spending.

India's curve was steepening for a more specific reason: abundant liquidity at shorter maturities. Measures introduced in June attracted more than $40 billion and could lift core rupee liquidity from INR5 trillion at end-June to INR10 trillion by December. The five-year government yield had fallen 35 basis points to 6.45%, versus a 17-basis-point decline in the 30-year to 7.47%, taking the gap above 100 basis points. Banks were putting cash into shorter assets while global inflation and supply concerns limited long-bond gains.

The RBI was expected to hold, with Governor Sanjay Malhotra seeing no broad-based inflation acceleration. The concessional deposit-swap window ends this quarter, however, giving the liquidity support a defined timetable. The steeper curve reflects that support for short bonds, not necessarily expectations of a more hawkish central bank.

Hong Kong's planned offshore hedging product became an operating market. Cash-settled five-year Chinese government-bond futures began trading with a CNY500,000 contract and an opening price only slightly different from the onshore equivalent. China's five-year government yield had closed Friday at 1.41%, its lowest since February 2025. After unsuccessful attempts in 2017 and 2024, the next question is whether sustained trading gives offshore investors a reliable hedge without requiring changes to their cash-bond holdings.

## African issuance broadens while Argentina waits

EM dollar bonds benefited from lower Treasury yields and oil even as the dollar strengthened. EMB gained 0.10% and the 15-year-plus dollar sovereign index rose 0.49%. The latter was still down 0.88% over a week and 3.54% over a month, leaving a substantial loss for longer-duration holders despite Monday's rebound.

African governments have continued to find financing. Citigroup arranged $6.2 billion of sovereign transactions in 2026, about 70% more than a year earlier and approaching its $7.3 billion total for all of 2025. Kenya, Angola and Ivory Coast tapped public or private markets, while Gabon's latest transaction raised $920 million. Earlier dollar weakness and risk appetite supported refinancing; renewed conflict remains a threat to the second-half calendar.

Official support is opening other routes. A UK Export Finance guarantee backs the GBP746 million redevelopment of Nigeria's Lagos and TinCan Island ports. A EUR2.7 billion railway from Kampala to the Kenyan border is being developed with potential World Bank participation. Guarantees and multilateral capital can make long-lived projects financeable at a time of high Treasury yields, while leaving implementation, currency and completion risks to be managed.

Argentina is choosing not to accept the external market's price. Investors were estimated to be willing to provide at least $5 billion, but Economy Minister Luis Caputo considered the roughly 9% yield inconsistent with the government's fiscal and inflation reforms. Instead, Argentina sold dollar-denominated bonds locally and obtained $3.2 billion of bank loans guaranteed by the World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank.

Those alternatives are cheaper, but the timing risk is considerable. Net reserves were estimated near $10 billion, the $20 billion IMF program requires rebuilding the cushion, and foreign-currency payments exceed $25 billion in 2027. Fiscal consolidation, agricultural exports and Vaca Muerta receipts help. Waiting nevertheless leaves more financing dependent on local dollars, multilaterals and a future market window that elections could make less favorable.

For Chile, the principal external variable is oil. June inflation accelerated to 4.3%, against a 3% target. Barclays estimated that a 10% oil increase adds about 5 basis points to the three-year peso sovereign yield. The policy rate implied one year ahead was 4.73%, roughly a quarter-point increase from 4.5%, whereas a cut had been priced a month earlier.

Monday's crude decline eases that pressure if it lasts. Chile's fuel-stabilization mechanism absorbs part of the difference between domestic and international prices, and the finance minister has warned that prolonged support would be unsustainable. Investors have shifted toward short inflation-linked UF bonds; 53% of survey respondents expected those yields to fall 1–10 basis points over the month. Sustained cheaper oil would help both inflation and the fiscal cost of cushioning consumers.

Brazil's easing expectations edged further out. The central bank's weekly survey lowered the end-2026 Selic forecast from 14% to 13.75%, while the inflation forecast fell for a fifth week to 5.03%. Policymakers were still expected to make a fourth consecutive 25-basis-point cut to 14%. Inflation remained well above the 3% target, leaving a gradual easing path rather than a rapid escape from restrictive rates.

## Stocks join the recovery, but credit funds lag

The S&P 500 rose 1.48%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.78% and semiconductors advanced 1.05%. VIX eased 0.81% to 15.86. Together with the Treasury rally, those moves showed investors welcoming lower geopolitical and energy risk rather than positioning for collapsing demand.

WTI at $80.32 and Brent at $83.86 were each still about 17% above month-earlier levels despite their steep daily declines. The ten-year breakeven fell only 1 basis point, a much smaller adjustment than crude's move. One diplomatic improvement had not erased the inflation consequences of the earlier rise in energy costs.

Gold rose 1.45% to $4,107.80 even as equities advanced, while the Dollar Index gained 0.22% to 100.017 after its prior-week decline. Demand for gold persisted through the broader recovery. US corporate funds' modest losses, against gains in Treasuries and EM dollar bonds, were the clearest limit to that recovery: easier benchmark rates had not produced a uniform bond-market bid.

## Refunding comes before the next labor-market test

Wednesday's refunding announcement follows the increase in Treasury's borrowing estimate to $739 billion. Unchanged coupon sizes would defer an immediate supply increase; language leaving room for February rather than May 2027 would bring the next adjustment closer. Investors need to distinguish that guidance from the demand subsequently shown at auctions.

The August 7 employment report will then test Williams's patience against the dissenters' preference for earlier tightening. Consensus calls for 85,000 additional payrolls after June's 57,000, with unemployment unchanged at 4.2%. Stronger hiring would reinforce the case for a September increase already assigned roughly 70% odds. Weaker labor demand would give the Fed more room to wait, particularly if the decline in real yields continued rather than relief remaining confined to energy prices.

Japan's intervention choices remain a separate Treasury risk. Borrowing through FIMA could limit outright sales, but repeated use of the capped, short-term facility would reveal the cost of sustaining that approach. The next BOJ meeting and any change to FIMA access will matter alongside the yen itself. Monday's diplomacy eased the immediate oil shock; it did not settle how Japan funds currency defense or how quickly domestic rates converge with those abroad.
